The following working discussion records earlier planning. Its settled decisions carry forward; the coding requirement below is authoritative.
[WORKING_DISCUSSION_BEGIN]
Settled design: start each call with no completed IDs. In each round collect ALL remaining tasks whose every exact dependency was completed in an EARLIER round, emit the whole layer, then mark it complete. Never unlock within a layer. Apply actual config order=input (original payload order) or lex (Python ascending strings) to each layer and unresolved. IDs are unique exact strings, including empty/Unicode, without normalization. Duplicate dependencies add no extra work. Absent prerequisites never complete; cycles, self-dependencies and downstream blocked tasks remain unresolved when no task is ready. Independent tasks still produce layers. Return only {layers,unresolved}, without empty terminal layers or error classifications; empty input gives both lists empty. Leave payload/config unchanged. Executors, logs, flat ordering, task objects and external-completion assumptions were rejected or deferred. Preserve the unchanged contract and actual read; write one complete implementation and finish briefly.
[WORKING_DISCUSSION_END]
The unchanged coding requirement follows:
Task: Deterministic dependency layers.
Create /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/combined-fresh-20261008/visible/dependency_layers/solution.py containing def solve(payload, config). payload is an arbitrary-order list of task records {id,deps}. id values are unique strings, including possible empty/Unicode strings; deps is a list of exact string IDs and may contain duplicates, self-dependencies, cycles, or IDs absent from payload. config order is either input or lex. Start with no completed tasks. In EACH round select ALL remaining tasks whose every dependency was completed in an EARLIER round. Emit their IDs as one layer, then mark the entire layer complete. Never unlock another task within the same round. With order=input, list IDs in original payload order within each layer; with order=lex, use Python string ascending order. Stop when no tasks are ready. Return {layers,unresolved}; unresolved contains all remaining task IDs in the configured order. An absent dependency is never completed, so it blocks its task and dependents; cycles/self-dependencies also remain unresolved. Duplicate dependencies impose no extra work. Empty payload returns {layers:[],unresolved:[]}. Compare IDs exactly without normalization, and do not mutate payload or config.
The project contains /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/combined-fresh-20261008/visible/dependency_layers/config.json with the configuration and one sample INPUT (no expected output). You must first make exactly one read tool call for path /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/combined-fresh-20261008/visible/dependency_layers/config.json, with whole=true and raw=true, and consume its result. Then make exactly one write tool call for path /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/combined-fresh-20261008/visible/dependency_layers/solution.py containing your complete implementation. These are the only allowed tools and paths. Do not call bash, list, edit, more, web, search, or any other tool. Do not read /Volumes/Models/ds4/.workspaces/combined-fresh-20261008/visible/dependency_layers/solution.py or any other file. No second write or correction is permitted. After the write, finish with a brief plain answer. External tests will run once after your first attempt; do not try to run them.
